title: conjur-intro declarative environment
description: Describes the end state of a Conjur environment so it can be provisioned reproducibly. This is the contract for bin/env: an unsupported or misspelled key is a hard error rather than a silent no-op. Every constraint lives here rather than in bin/env, so a hand-written spec fails the same way a generated one does, and the accepted range of each field widens only as bin/env learns to build it -- a spec that validates is a spec that can be provisioned. See docs/declarative-environments.md.

version.description: Appliance image tag to provision, as passed to `bin/dap --version`. Must be a quoted string: unquoted `13.5` is a YAML number, and unquoted `13.10` would silently become 13.1. The pattern is docker's own tag grammar, and it matters because this value reaches a command line.

leader.description: The leader and its standby cluster.

standbys.description: Number of standbys to deploy alongside the leader. Only 0 validates today, because bin/env does not provision standbys yet. The ceiling rises to 4 -- the number of conjur-master services docker-compose.yml defines -- when it does.

auto_failover.description: Enrol the leader and its standbys in an auto-failover cluster. Only false validates today. Auto-failover, and the constraint that it needs at least 2 standbys to hold a quorum, arrive together with standby support.

followers.description: Number of followers to deploy behind the follower load balancer. Only 0 validates today, because bin/env does not provision followers yet. The ceiling rises to 1 when it does, and beyond that once multi-follower compose services exist.

sample_data.description: Load the sample policy and variable values. Defaults to true: with no policy and no secrets there is nothing to reproduce a secret-retrieval issue against.

events.description: RESERVED SEAM -- NOT IMPLEMENTED. A large share of real escalations are about transitions (an upgrade, a promotion, a triggered failover) rather than an end state, and bin/dap already models those as discrete actions. Reserving the key now means adding them later is an extension rather than a breaking redesign. Only an empty list validates today; see docs/declarative-environments.md.
